title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free

items.title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free
items.statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty connected smooth manifold, let $E,A,\kappa\in C^\infty(X,\mathbb R)$, and let $C>0$ be a constant with $\kappa(x)>0$ for every $x\in X$. Here $dE$ and $dA$ are the differential one-forms of the indicated functions, and equality of one-forms means pointwise equality on $X$. Assume the classical first-law product identity
$$dE=C\kappa\,dA.$$
For every constant $b>0$ and offset $s_*\in\mathbb R$, set $T_b:=b\kappa$ and $S_{b,s_*}:=(C/b)A+s_*$. Then $T_b dS_{b,s_*}=dE$. Distinct positive $b$ give distinct functions $T_b$, and changing $s_*$ changes $S_{b,s_*}$ without changing its differential. Thus this product identity alone does not determine the temperature scale or the absolute entropy offset.

The names $T_b$ and $S_{b,s_*}$ denote real-valued functions here; no operational temperature or physical entropy is assumed. If the symbols carry dimensions, consistency requires $[T]=[b][\kappa]$, $[S]=[C][A]/[b]$, and $[E]=[T][S]$. No particular unit system is used.

references.title: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Introduction to black hole thermodynamics, 78-page lecture notes, §§1.3 and 2.1, arXiv:2512.24929v1
Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6, §§2–3, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119v2

title: Classical first-law product leaves entropy-temperature calibration free — Examples

items.title: Two entropy-temperature calibrations preserve the same energy differential
items.statement: Use the abstract state family $X=(0,\infty)$ with coordinate $r$, and define $E(r)=r$, $A(r)=r$, $\kappa(r)=1$, and $C=1$. These are formal real-valued functions with no physical units assigned. Then $dE=C\kappa\,dA=dr$. The choices $b=1$ and $b=2$, with offset $s_*=0$, give $(T_1,S_{1,0})=(1,r)$ and $(T_2,S_{2,0})=(2,r/2)$.

references.title: Pietro Benetti Genolini, Introduction to black hole thermodynamics, 78-page lecture notes, §§1.3 and 2.1, arXiv:2512.24929v1
Robert M. Wald, The Thermodynamics of Black Holes, Living Reviews in Relativity 4 (2001), 6, §§2–3, arXiv:gr-qc/9912119v2

items.title: Identical geometry and energy data with different finite quantum entropy
items.statement:
On the complex Hilbert space $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$, a density matrix means a positive semidefinite $2\times2$ matrix $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$. Let the Hamiltonian be the zero self-adjoint matrix $H=0$, define its energy by $E_H(\rho)=\operatorname{Tr}(\rho H)$, fix one geometric datum $a>0$, and fix a positive scalar $k_B>0$. Define the finite spectral entropy by
$$S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_{\lambda\in\operatorname{spec}(\rho)}\lambda\log\lambda,$$
where eigenvalues are counted with multiplicity, $\log$ is the natural logarithm, and $0\log0:=0$. The statement that the fixed data $(a,E_H(\rho))=(a,0)$ determine one value of $S(\rho)$ for every density matrix $\rho$ on $\mathcal H$ is false.

The scalar $a$ is held fixed as a mathematical label; $H$ is only the displayed finite matrix. No physical units, dynamics, horizon state, or coupling to geometry is part of this construction.
